title: Find Your Passion in 20 Minutes, Not 20 Years
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Host promotes his own paid AI agency program (pitches charging local businesses $500-$5,000/month, teaches cold SMS/cold-call outreach) and his own free Obsession Audit tool (obsessionaudit.com). Most other businesses are one-line mentions with no numbers; the only figures for the miniature-house Kickstarter are second-hand.

idea.name: Obsession Audit tool
idea.one_liner: Free vibe-coded web tool at obsessionaudit.com that uses AI on a person's YouTube history, search history, Amazon orders and bank statements to surface their hidden obsessions.
idea.customer: People trying to find their passion or business direction
idea.offer: AI-guided self-audit of personal data exports and prompts
idea.revenue_model: Free (no monetisation stated; likely a lead magnet for the podcast)

key_quotes.quote: I need to buy that domain name, actually.
I mean, this can be a business.

ideas.delivery: Self-serve web app built with vibe coding; workflow uploads data exports (Google Takeout, Amazon order export, bank statements) to an LLM

idea.name: AI consulting for local businesses
idea.one_liner: Set up and manage AI tools (voice agents, automations) for local businesses on a $500-$5,000/month retainer.
idea.offer: Setup and ongoing management of AI tools, voice agents and automations

key_quotes.quote: show you how to start an AI consulting business where you can charge local businesses $500 to $5,000 a month to set up and manage AI tools for them.
This is stuff you can just copy, paste and deploy for clients on day one.
You also get my frameworks for cold email, Facebook ads, SMS, cold calls.

claims.claim: Can charge local businesses $500-$5,000 per month
claims.quote: show you how to start an AI consulting business where you can charge local businesses $500 to $5,000 a month to set up and manage AI tools for them.

acquisition_channels.details: Cold email frameworks supplied by the program
Lead spreadsheets of businesses in your niche and area

ideas.delivery: Consultant deploys template automations, Claude Code builds and AI voice agents for each client and manages them ongoing

uk_legal_risk.reason: The taught acquisition relies partly on cold SMS to local businesses, many of which are sole traders or partnerships. PECR bans unsolicited marketing texts to them, cold email is only allowed to limited companies, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR (client customer data handled by AI tools, call recording by voice agents); PECR for any automated outbound calls made by voice agents for clients

idea.name: Stakes-based accountability app
idea.one_liner: App where users connect a credit card (and accounts like their inbox) and are automatically charged, e.g. a donation to charity, if they miss a goal.
idea.offer: Goal tracking with automatic financial penalties verified through integrations
idea.revenue_model: Not stated (could be subscription or a cut of forfeited stakes)

key_quotes.quote: And business idea, someone needs to invent an app that like productizes that stakes, right?
Where you like, you connect your credit card, and it's like, hey, maybe you connect your inbox as well.
if I don't get to inbox zero, every Tuesday by 3 p.m., don't eight hundred dollars to this charity or whatever.

claims.claim: Host staked $100 per team member to force himself to film videos
claims.quote: I will give each of you guys a hundred bucks.

claims.claim: Example stake: $800 to charity for missing inbox zero
claims.quote: if I don't get to inbox zero, every Tuesday by 3 p.m., don't eight hundred dollars to this charity or whatever.

ideas.delivery: Self-serve app with payment and inbox integrations that verify goals and trigger charges automatically
ideas.other_uk_rules: FCA payment services/e-money rules if holding user stakes; Gambling Act 2005 risk if stakes could be won back or paid to other users; UK GDPR for inbox access; DMCC Act subscription rules; Consumer Rights Act fairness of penalty terms
